items.name: Ghidra
items.description: An extensible reverse-engineering suite with disassembly and decompilation features for inspecting compiled game code.
items.source_evidence: The NSA-maintained project describes Ghidra as a software reverse-engineering framework and lists disassembly and decompilation among its capabilities.

items.name: decomp.me
items.description: A browser-based collaborative workspace for matching individual functions with project-specific compiler presets.
items.source_evidence: The official site calls itself a collaborative reverse-engineering platform; its FAQ explains the role of compiler, platform, and build settings in project scratches.

items.name: objdiff
items.description: A local GUI for comparing rebuilt object files against target objects and inspecting function and data differences.
items.source_evidence: The project README describes object-file comparison, automatic rebuilds, progress reporting, and support for several console CPU families.

items.name: N64: Recompiled
items.description: A toolchain that statically recompiles N64 binaries into C for building native ports and related projects.
items.source_evidence: The maintainer README describes the binary-to-C workflow and notes that symbol/build metadata is required; it is not a one-click port generator.

items.name: Proton
items.description: Valve's Steam compatibility tool for running many Windows PC games on Linux, built around Wine and additional components.
items.source_evidence: Valve's repository describes Proton's Windows-game-on-Linux purpose and documents its Wine basis and graphics components such as DXVK and vkd3d-proton.

items.name: DXVK
items.description: A Vulkan-based implementation of Direct3D 8, 9, 10, and 11 used with Wine and in compatibility stacks such as Proton.
items.source_evidence: The project README states the Direct3D versions and Vulkan target, and explains use through Wine and Steam Play tools.

items.name: vkd3d-proton
items.description: A Proton-focused implementation of Direct3D 12 on Vulkan, complementary to DXVK's Direct3D 8–11 coverage.
items.source_evidence: The upstream README describes the project as implementing Direct3D 12 on Vulkan and as the development effort behind Proton's D3D12 support.

items.name: Floating IPS (Flips)
items.description: A desktop and command-line patcher for creating and applying IPS and BPS patches, useful for distributing fan-made changes without bundling a game image.
items.source_evidence: The maintainer README documents IPS/BPS creation and application, GUI and command-line use, and release downloads.

items.name: GameBanana
items.description: A cross-game community site for discovering and publishing mods, tools, and other game-specific submissions.
items.source_evidence: GameBanana's community guide describes game-specific modding communities, submissions, and volunteer game managers; the live homepage showed active trending and recent community content.

items.name: ProtonDB
items.description: Crowdsourced game-by-game reports and workarounds for running Steam titles through Proton on Linux and Steam Deck.
items.source_evidence: The site's own overview explains its user-submitted Proton compatibility reports, aggregate ratings, and game-specific suggestions; recent game reports were visible.

items.name: Data Crystal
items.description: A community-maintained reference for ROM-hacking knowledge, including game-specific ROM/RAM maps, notes, formats, and technical discoveries.
items.source_evidence: The wiki describes itself as a cross-system repository of ROM-hacking knowledge and presents console- and game-specific reference pages.

items.name: The Cutting Room Floor
items.description: A community wiki documenting cut, unused, debug, prototype, and regional-variation content that can inform preservation and mod research.
items.source_evidence: The site's own description identifies its focus on unused and debug content, development history, and prototypes; its game-data category was indexed on the verification date.

items.name: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
items.description: An open-source MCP server and CLI that lets coding agents inspect websites, Electron applications, and native binaries with local analysis tools, returning findings with evidence and limitations.
items.source_evidence: The project README describes REA as an agent-connected reverse-engineering tool for websites, applications, and native binaries; it says analysis runs locally and returns evidence and limitations. The repository is public, MIT-licensed, and has a release published 2026-10-14.
